t: For pay, allowances, individual clothing, subsistence interest on deposits, gratuities, permanent change of station travel (including all expenses thereof for organizational movements), and expenses of temporary duty travel between permanent duty stations, for members of the Marine Corps on active duty (except members of the Reserve provided for elsewhere); $1,396,300,000.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriation for Marine Corps military personnel pay, allowances, and travel. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. The only people referenced are active-duty Marines, who are federal personnel receiving pay, not participants in a federal decision.
fable.s: for members of the Marine Corps on active duty (except members of the Reserve provided for elsewhere); $1,396,300,000.

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard appropriations clause authorizing funds for the pay and travel expenses of Marine Corps members. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. The actors involved are federal employees (Marines) and the funding mechanism itself, which falls under internal government operations.
qwen_block.s: For pay, allowances, individual clothing, subsistence interest on deposits, gratuities, permanent change of station travel (including all expenses thereof for organizational movements), and expenses of temporary duty travel between permanent duty stations, for members of the Marine Corps on active duty (except members of the Reserve provided for elsewhere); $1,396,300,000.

opus.w: This section only appropriates $1,396,300,000 for Marine Corps pay, allowances, travel and related costs. No party outside the federal government is consulted or given a role in any federal decision. Like the funding provision in Example 1, it describes money and how it may be used, not a process for outside input.
opus.b: This is a "No," and there isn't really a tempting "Yes" reading. The section is a plain appropriation for Marine Corps pay and travel. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard appropriation clause authorizing funds for the pay, allowances, and travel expenses of active-duty Marine Corps members. Active-duty military personnel are federal employees, so their compensation does not constitute participation by outside parties. There is no requirement for consultation, public comment, or coordination with non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: For pay, allowances, individual clothing, subsistence interest on deposits, gratuities, permanent change of station travel (including all expenses thereof for organizational movements), and expenses of temporary duty travel between permanent duty stations, for members of the Marine Corps on active duty (except members of the Reserve provided for elsewhere); $1,396,300,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "members of the Marine Corps" are outside the federal government because they are individuals, but this is incorrect. Military personnel on active duty are federal employees. The section is purely an appropriation for their compensation and travel, involving no consultation, coordination, or decision-making input from outside parties.
